        - heading "Understand Chi-Square Independence" [level=2]
        - paragraph: A chi-square independence test checks whether two categorical variables are associated. You can learn Chi-Square Independence by trying one small example instead of long theory.
        - paragraph: Use a two-way table, compute expected counts from margins, then compare observed and expected counts. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, sport and grade: Check whether sport choice is associated with grade. Watch out: Treating association as proof of cause. A chi-square test can show association, not prove cause by itself."
